AK02.question: Give two tests to detect whether my left index finger lets go before a slow L turn is complete. Let the tests take at most 61 seconds in total, with headings in the form “name: seconds”. Then, in a separate paragraph, give one sentence asking Sam to flag the early releases in my video.

value.answer:
Here are two quick tests for whether your left index finger releases the L face before a slow L turn finishes. Total time: 61 seconds.

**Mirror check: 30 seconds**
Do slow L turns in front of a mirror (or phone front camera) for 30 seconds, watching the fingertip against the L-face stickers. If the finger lifts off while the face is still rotating, you have an early release.

**Sticker-contact count: 31 seconds**
For 31 seconds, do slow L turns and count aloud each turn where the fingertip stays in contact until the face stops. Compare that count with the total turns; any turn where contact ends early is a release before completion.

Sam, please flag the early releases in my video.

Here are two quick tests for whether your left index finger releases the L face before a slow L turn finishes.

Video frame check: 30 seconds
Record one slow L turn at a high frame rate, then step through the frames and note the frame where the L face stops moving and the frame where your left index finger first lifts off; if the lift comes earlier, the finger released early.

Mirror-and-pause drill: 31 seconds
Do a slow L turn in front of a mirror (or phone camera) and freeze at the moment the turn feels finished; if your left index finger is already off the cube at that freeze point, it let go before the turn was complete.

Sam, please flag the early releases in my video.

AK03.question: I am checking if my right thumb slips across a sticker while the other hand takes over. Write two untimed grip-transfer drills with a visible stop point in each. Also, in a new paragraph, write one sentence inviting Noor to compare the clips on Thursday.

value.answer:
Here are two untimed grip-transfer drills, each with a clear visible stop point so you can check whether your right thumb slides across a sticker during the handover.

Drill 1 — Slow R-to-L handover on a single face turn
- Hold the cube with your right thumb on the front-right sticker and your left hand on the left face.
- Turn the right face slowly with your right hand only, watching the thumb contact point.
- Stop point: pause the moment your left hand grips the cube to take over, with the cube held still and your right thumb still touching the same sticker.
- Check: look at whether the thumb has shifted relative to that sticker; if it has, the slip happened during the transfer, not the turn.

Drill 2 — Alternating two-hand regrip
- Start with both hands in a neutral grip, then alternate small turns, passing control back and forth between hands.
- Stop point: after each handover, freeze completely for a count of two with both hands still on the cube, then inspect the right thumb's position against its sticker before continuing.
- Check: repeat until you can complete several handovers with the thumb staying on the same sticker each time.

Noor, could you compare the clips on Thursday?

Here are two untimed grip-transfer drills, each with a clear visible stop point so you can check whether your right thumb slides across a sticker during the handover.

Drill 1 — Slow-motion transfer with a pause
- Hold the cube in your normal solving grip and turn the right face slowly with your right hand until the thumb is about to release.
- Transfer the grip to your left hand and stop completely the moment the left hand has taken the cube.
- Visible stop point: freeze with the cube held only by the left hand, right hand lifted clear and open, for a full two seconds.
- Look at where your right thumb was resting: if it has drifted onto a different sticker than where it started, the slip happened during the transfer.
- Repeat ten times, resetting the thumb to the same starting sticker each time.

Drill 2 — Sticker-marked checkpoint
- Put a small removable marker (a dot of tape or a sticker) on the exact sticker your right thumb normally contacts.
- Perform a slow sequence that requires one handover, and pause at the handover.
- Visible stop point: stop with the marked sticker facing you and the cube supported only by the taking hand, then check whether the mark is still under where your thumb was.
- If the mark has moved relative to your thumb's contact point, your thumb slid; if it stayed put, the transfer was clean.
- Do five repetitions, then remove the marker.

In both drills the pause is the point: it makes the slip visible instead of letting it hide inside continuous turning.

Noor, could you compare the clips on Thursday?

To check whether the slip comes from sideways thumb drag during the handoff, keep both drills untimed and treat each stop point as a still checkpoint you can see.

- **Drill 1 — Straight-lift freeze:** Rest the pad of your right thumb on a front sticker while the left hand cradles the cube. Slowly reduce right-thumb pressure as the left hand takes the load, then lift the right thumb straight up and freeze it about a centimetre above the same sticker. Visible stop: the thumb hovers over that sticker without sideways travel and the cube has not rotated; hold the still shape, then set the thumb back down and repeat.
- **Drill 2 — Planted-thumb handoff:** Start with the right thumb planted on a front sticker and the left hand loose at the side. Bring the left hand in to take support, and stop as soon as the left fingers are set while the right thumb is still on its original sticker. Visible stop: both hands are in contact, the right thumb pad is centred on the same sticker, and there is a clear gap between the thumb tip and the next sticker edge; pause there, then withdraw the right thumb straight up.

Noor, please compare the clips on Thursday.
